title: tune-nccl-overlap-scheduling-and-stream-priorities-for-tensor-parallel
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: tensor-parallel (TP) workloads showed suboptimal overlap between NCCL collectives and GPU compute in high-concurrency serving. This PR introduces a scheduling and stream-priority tuning pass in the runtime to increase communication/computation overlap for TP collective patterns. Summary of changes: 1) add per-device per-collective stream pool and assign priorities so compute kernels launch on high-priority compute streams while NCCL collectives use dedicated comm streams; 2) introduce async event-based handoff (non-blocking cudaEvent recording + streamWait) to avoid implicit stream synchronizations introduced by earlier sync paths; 3) refine heuristics that pick when to colocate kernels with comm based on sequence-length distribution and KV-cache hit rates; 4) expose a runtime flag to control aggressive overlap heuristics and fall back to previous behavior on regressions; 5) perf test harness and docs describing tuning knobs. Design notes: the change keeps public APIs unchanged; it operates purely in the serving runtime's scheduler layer and NCCL manager. We add conservative defaults to preserve stability for Dedicated/Private customers. Results: on internal perf lab (A100s, 4xTP model, typical production sequence mix) we observed 12-18% throughput uplift under latency-constrained workloads and 8-10% token-cost reduction from improved batching. Tests: added unit tests for the new scheduler paths and an integration perf test that simulates mixed-length traffic. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind runtime flag, perf monitoring dashboard added to Console to detect regressions. Backwards compatibility: no model or API changes; opt-in aggressive heuristics and immediate rollback via flag if issues observed.
